Messages.Author: Andrew S. Davidson
Messages.Body:
The Clan Elders variant looks interesting but its outright ban on
vampires of 5 or less capacity is not to my taste. It has sparked an
idea for another variant and I'm jotting the details down here before
I forget. This is an untested draft - caveat emptor.

Circle of Death
---------------

1. The general rules level is as per Sabbat Wars except as noted
below.

2. Each player starts with a single active Inner Circle vampire at
full capacity. These are chosen in sequence and no two players may
have the same choice. They also start with 30 pool and 4 inactive
vampires as usual.

3. This Inner Circle vampire represents the player themselves - this
time, it's personal. Player are not ousted if they lose all their
pool. Instead, they are ousted if their Inner Circle member is burnt.

4. There are two ways to win.

a) By being the last survivor.

b) By accumulating 60 pool. If time expires, the player
with the most pool is the winner.

5. You may still only bleed to the left. Any pool which is bled goes
to the successful bleeder's pool - it does not go to the bank.

6. The Inner Circle members may not transfer their own blood to their
pool (e.g. no Minion Tap in this case). Instead, they may choose to
use their own blood to pay any pool costs incurred by Master cards and
the like.

7. Players may not take control of another player's Inner Circle
member, e.g. no Hostile Takeover in this case.

8. There is no rule 8.

9. No poofters.

------------------------------------------------------------------

The objectives of this variant include:

i) To increase the role-playing affinity between the player and his
oldest vampire. You can still play weenies but they should only be
cannon fodder, not the heart of your strategy.

ii) To make voting locks more difficult.

iii) To provide a positive victory condition which does not require
you to eliminate every other player.

iv) To give the players a running start which will enable the playing
of a wide variety of discipline cards, so encouraging a more varied
library.

v) to provide a better arena for vampire vs vampire combat - defending
the inner circle member will be a sine qua non.

So, would this work mechanically? I think there's enough there to
stop obvious abuses like immediate Minion Tap/5th Trad but am not sure
if I've missed some other broken combos.

Andrew

Messages.Author: Derek Ray
Messages.Body:
On Fri, 08 Dec 2000 15:47:06 +0000, Andrew S. Davidson <a...@csi.com>
wrote:

[variant snipped]

>So, would this work mechanically? I think there's enough there to
>stop obvious abuses like immediate Minion Tap/5th Trad but am not sure
>if I've missed some other broken combos.

Inner Circle members can't play 5th Tradition, so you would have to
bring out a Prince. No worries there.

What you DO have to worry about, though, is:

Turn #1: I make 1 transfer to Olivia (POT OBF vic).
Turn #2: I make 4 transfers and bring out Olivia.
Turn #3: Olivia plays Bum's Rush and Forgotten Labyrinth, targeting
your IC Member. Now she plays Torn Signpost, Immortal Grapple,
Disarm, and Amaranth. Your IC member is burned, and you are ousted.
Olivia goes away in the Blood Hunt, but it was worth it.

I make 1 transfer to the second, third, and fourth copies of Olivia in
my crypt.

Turn #4: I make 4 transfers and bring out Olivia...

Anyway, I'm sure you see how this plays out. Stealth-Rush becomes the
order of the day, and it's very difficult to stop someone who's
willing to suicidally nuke themselves. The IC members without
Fortitude begin to suffer the worst, as they haven't even got the
option to prevent.

There was a variant much like this posted somewhere previously;
perhaps on Mark Langsdorf's page? Or maybe LSJ would know. I've seen
something like this before, and that was the big problem with it then,
too. There was an elaborate setup to get around it, but I'm not sure
what it was.

-- Derek

I see the problem. My thinking was that all players would be taking
extreme measures to protect themselves and I supposed that, with an
appropriate library, there'd be enough stoppers. Isn't Obedience a
good counter - your IC member should usually have the advantage of
seniority.

The other issue would be whether you'd leave yourself too open if you
put a lot of resources into a suicide rush. I was hoping for a
opening period of maneuvering for advantage as happens in L5R and
Shadowfist.

Anyway, if this has been done before, I'm all ears. Is there a
repository of such variants to save me from reinventing the wheel?

Andrew

Harrod and Gwendolyn don't have Dominate, so they'd be at a
disadvantage there. The other half is that I might well just send
Harrod over on the first turn, since he has POT/CEL, and play Torn
Signpost/Increased Strength/IG/Blur. This hits you for 6 on the first

that didn't have it. That could be very messy.

take (D) actions against your opponent's IC member/Justicar if your
opponent has any other ready vampires." This would help the Olivia
case and the Rush problem in general, but wouldn't do much for when
Harrod came over on turn 1. You could bar your IC member from taking
any actions, of course, and that would neatly fix the opening-turn
rush; but does that remove much of the flavor of the variant?

>The other issue would be whether you'd leave yourself too open if you
>put a lot of resources into a suicide rush. I was hoping for a
>opening period of maneuvering for advantage as happens in L5R and
>Shadowfist.

At 30 pool, 5 pool for Olivia is pretty insignificant, especially if
you gain 6 for ousting someone. This is one of the strengths of
weenie hordes; they rarely spend more than 10 pool on their first 4-5
vampires, so even though they usually lack defense, 20+ pool takes a
long time to bleed or vote through.

>Anyway, if this has been done before, I'm all ears. Is there a
>repository of such variants to save me from reinventing the wheel?

White Wolf's website, maybe. LSJ might know. Or Judith and Mark's
page, although I'm not familiar with the actual link. The Lasombra
probably knows, as well.

Something like:

Round 1:

Minion Tap for about 7
GtU +2 bleed
Command of the Beast (sup) +1
Conditioning +3
IC bleed bonus +2
stealth to taste.
Pool total after round 1: 30+7+9 = 46

Master:Discipline Card (or nothing or something productive)

Command of the Beast (sup) +1
Conditioning +3

margin of error.

Sure you win and get ousted at the same time, but you should be able to

survival should be expected.

Messages.Author: Derek Ray
Messages.Body:
On Sat, 09 Dec 2000 13:05:40 -0600, James Hamblin
<ham...@math.wisc.edu> wrote:

>
>Sadly, Burning Wrath is not a hand strike, and thus cannot be used under
>Immortal Grapple. Sorry to be the bearer of sad tidings...

How remarkable. I don't think I'd ever checked out the new online
text, and the DS text on the card reads "Strike: +1 hand damage,
aggravated." The original Undead Strength, Growing Fury, Mighty
Grapple, and Pushing the Limit texts read: "Strike: Use your hand or
melee weapon", so I can easily see where the Rules Team made the
differentiation between one and the other. An excellent case for
altering the wording to "strength" to avoid messy bits like this,
especially since Dark Sovereigns contained no other Potence strike
cards to directly compare the wording to.

I am curious as to WHY the Rules Team chose to make that particular
differentiation, although I expect the reasons are either obvious
("interpreted as printed") or lost in history now. It doesn't seem to
make sense for Potence to have a close-range strike based directly on
strength ("hand damage") that isn't actually a hand strike; its only
other close-range strikes are Fractured Armament and Shattering Blow,
neither of which are based on strength. Its other strikes (Gate, Lid,
Car, Carnage) are all ranged and therefore unconfusable.

A shame, though. Burning Wrath seemed borderline even WITH the
ability to Grab someone; 3 blood is far too much now, IMO, for a
strike that really needs to be paired with Celerity and a 2nd or 3rd
strike.

Messages.Author: LSJ
Messages.Body:
James Hamblin <ham...@math.wisc.edu> wrote:
> LSJ wrote:
> >
> > Correct. Burning Wrath is a hand strike (as is Scorpion Sting, for
> > that matter).
>
> Wow, I must be on crack. Was this card (before the Age of LSJ)
> originally not considered a hand strike?

Yes. At one time, neither Scorpion Sting nor Burning Wrath were
hand strikes, since neither said "use your hand...". Eventually
Tom said that the desin intent of Scorpion Sting was that it
should be a hand strike, and later still Jon Wilkie clarified
that Burning Wrath was a hand strike (since it didn't "involve
weapons").

When the definition of hand strikes was formalized, they remained
hand strikes, by the definition.
